during taxi out for departure, we experience some brief brake chatter during our last turn prior to the runway. while awaiting takeoff clearance, we set the parking brake and received an amber brk fail caution. we called ops and mcc, then shut the aircraft down and called the fbo for a tow back to the ramp. a ground reset procedure was not accomplished because the issue occurred well after start up and taxi out.   reset brakes. ops check good. iaw phenom 300 amm 31-31-00

the rt side pitot system becomes blocked, with the symptom being the right pfd (and standby) airspeed slowly drops to 0. maintenance has checked the probe heat repeatedly and found no defects. this has happened to me on at least two different pc12s. my theory is that water enters the pitot system and freezes before it can drain out, as the system recovers when descending through the freezing level.
nr 2 eng aft mount has chipped material on upper surface, fll-0035, ata 71. accomplished repair per eo-97541-req1 and vt-saa ea 757-7121-01-b0744 rev i/r.

aircraft was grounded: an emergency was declared into dfw due to the flight crew reporting at 31000 they had flap lock flashing until the flaps were moved to flaps 2. they also reported recieving a wing tip locked ecam. the flight crew accomplished a go around and accomplished the ecam procedures. at flaps 3 the indication cleared itself. the aircraft landed safely at dfw without further incident. maintenance found the blue and green hydraulic systems were low and the yellow sytem was overserviced. maintenance serviced all 3 hydraulic systems per amm 12-12-29. a satisfactory operational check

during approach, the flight crew reported that the landing gear handle was selected down but emergency extension procedures were followed to allow the landing gear to be extended safely. maintenance reported that upon inspection it was noted that the hydraulic fluid level was below the minimum cold acceptable level and serviced the system. they inspected for any other abnormalities and all else was good. landing gear extension and retraction checks were successfully performed, and the aircraft was returned to service.
